profile.summary: This is the third edition of the Livesey and Marsh benchmark of missense variant effect predictors. It ranks 97 predictors by how well their scores correlate with deep mutational scanning measurements in 36 human proteins, and separately ranks 83 predictors by how well they separate ClinVar pathogenic from gnomAD population missense variants in 819 proteins. Rankings are pairwise: each predictor's score is its average win rate against every other predictor on the variants both of them score.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things. First, agreement between a predictor's scores and experimental fitness measurements from deep mutational scanning, using absolute Spearman correlation, because only a monotonic relationship is needed. Second, discrimination between pathogenic and population missense variants in clinical data, using AUROC per protein. The authors' premise is that a predictor consistent across many functional assays is the most useful one, and they report that relative performance on the assay benchmark predicts relative performance on the clinical one for predictors not trained on human clinical variants.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, Comparison of VEP performance using DMS data; Abstract

quotes.text: We use absolute Spearman’s rank correlation to assess the correspondence between VEPs and DMS, as only a monotonic relationship between the two variables is required.
the premise of our analysis is that VEPs that show the most consistency across a large set of DMS experiments are likely to be the most useful for predicting variant effects

We observe a strong correspondence between VEP performance in DMS-based benchmarks and clinical variant classification, especially for predictors that have not been directly trained on human clinical variants.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The assay set starts from the 26 datasets of the previous edition, removes every variant also present in the authors' ClinVar and gnomAD sets, then keeps only datasets with at least 1000 scored amino acid variants. Datasets measuring antibody binding or unrelated binding affinity, and those without methodological details, were excluded; 13 new datasets, mostly from MaveDB, were added, giving 36 proteins and 207,460 single amino acid variants. One score set per protein is used, chosen as the one with the highest median Spearman correlation across all predictors. The clinical set takes ClinVar missense variants (downloaded 06/08/2024) labelled pathogenic, likely pathogenic or pathogenic/likely pathogenic, drops 0-star entries and entries with conflicting interpretations, and uses gnomAD v4.1 missense variants that pass the genomes or exomes filters as a putatively benign class. Proteins with at least 10 of each class qualify, giving 819 proteins.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: For each protein, the absolute Spearman correlation with the assay is computed for every pair of predictors using only variants all three (assay and both predictors) score. The predictor with the higher correlation wins the comparison. Win rates are pooled over proteins and the rank score is the average win rate against all other predictors. The clinical ranking uses the same pairwise procedure with AUROC in place of Spearman, and a parallel version uses AUPRC. Predictors that score low for pathogenic are inverted by subtracting from 1. Error bars on the assay ranking are the standard deviation of the rank score over 1000 bootstraps resampling 36 protein datasets with replacement; error bars on the clinical ranking are the standard error across comparisons.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: Download the prediction files and the scripts from the three figshare records and run the two Python scripts. Figures_1_and_2.py rebuilds the assay benchmark from the per-protein prediction CSVs, the DMS summary, the ClinVar and gnomAD variant files and the renaming and inversion rules; Figure 3.py rebuilds the clinical ranking from the variant score file. Paths at the top of each script must be set first.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: 36 human deep mutational scanning datasets covering 207,460 single amino acid variants (one score set per protein), and a clinical set of ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic versus gnomAD v4.1 putatively benign missense variants across 819 proteins.

quotes.text: across 36 proteins and covering 207,460 different single amino acid variants
We generated predictions for 819 proteins that had at least 10 (likely) pathogenic and 10 putatively benign missense variants

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: No train, validation or test split: all data are evaluation data, and the predictors are external tools. Variants present in ClinVar or gnomAD are removed from the assay benchmark, and datasets were excluded for predictors trained on that assay data.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Results, Comparison of VEP performance using DMS data

quotes.text: allowed us to exclude all variants present in ClinVar and gnomAD from calculations of Spearman’s correlation
we have excluded specific proteins from the assessment of predictors that were trained using DMS data, to avoid potential data circularity

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Assay benchmark: pairwise win rate on absolute Spearman correlation (higher is better). Clinical benchmark: pairwise win rate on AUROC, with an AUPRC version in the supplement (higher is better).

quotes.text: We use absolute Spearman’s rank correlation to assess the correspondence between VEPs and DMS
using AUROC as our comparison metric instead of Spearman’s correlation
The same procedure was used to generate the AUPRC-based ranking in Additional file 1: Fig. S4, but with precision-recall instead of ROC.

facts.label: Baselines
facts.value: The predictors are the comparison set: 97 in the assay benchmark and 83 in the clinical one, grouped as clinical-trained (46), population-free (31) and population-tuned (6). 27 came from dbNSFP 4.2; the rest were run locally, downloaded, taken from web interfaces or from ProteinGym.

quotes.text: served as a source for 27 VEPs.
The remaining 70 VEPs were either run locally on the University of Edinburgh high performance computing cluster (EDDIE)
using 46 clinical-trained, 31 population-free, and 6 population-tuned VEPs

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: For the assay benchmark: all ClinVar and gnomAD variants are removed, and proteins are excluded for predictors trained on that assay. For the clinical benchmark: none. The authors state they made no effort to exclude training variants there and that clinical-trained predictors are likely inflated by circularity.

quotes.text: allowed us to exclude all variants present in ClinVar and gnomAD from calculations of Spearman’s correlation
is highly inflated by circularity issues, as we made no effort to exclude variants used in training

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: 1000 bootstraps resampling the 36 protein datasets with replacement give the standard deviation of each assay rank score; the clinical ranking reports the standard error across pairwise comparisons.

facts.label: Assays
facts.value: Deep mutational scanning, classified as direct (measuring the protein's own function) or indirect (for example growth or complementation). Clinical labels come from ClinVar assertions and gnomAD allele observations, not assays.

quotes.text: DMS datasets are classified as “direct” if they directly measure the ability of the target protein to carry out one or more functions, with all others being classified as “indirect.”

facts.label: Allowed inputs
facts.value: Inapplicable: the benchmark scores whatever each published predictor produces and does not restrict inputs. Coverage differs between predictors, with some scoring only substitutions reachable by a single nucleotide change.

limitations.text: A rank score is relative, not absolute: it depends on which other predictors are in the comparison and is not a correlation or an AUROC.
limitations.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Spearman's correlation and rank score

quotes.text: The win rate of every VEP over every other VEP was then calculated across all proteins by dividing the number of wins by the number of times that particular pair of VEPs were tested.

limitations.text: The clinical ranking excludes no training variants, so the authors say clinical-trained predictors are likely inflated there by circularity.

notes: This is the 2025 edition (Genome Biology 26:104), the third after the 2020 and 2023 Molecular Systems Biology papers; the earlier editions used other assay sets, predictor sets and, in 2020, another ranking method. size for the assay entry is the whole set (207,460 variants across 36 proteins), as the article gives no separate test count; size for the clinical entry counts qualifying proteins, not variants, because the article gives no variant total. There is no leaderboard, so results_url is null; per-predictor rank scores are in Additional file 2. The store holds further assay protocols (SNV-accessible only, gaps filled, direct assays only, indirect assays only) that this page describes only in general terms. The scripts and prediction files were downloaded from the figshare addresses in the data availability statement.
